issue_title: [Bug]: stm32h5xx_hal_spi.c does not operate correctly in blocking mode when optimised
clean_text:
Title: [Bug]: stm32h5xx_hal_spi.c does not operate correctly in blocking mode when optimised

Body:
### Bug Summary

If stm32h5xx_hal_spi.c optimisation is set to -Og artifacts are generated in u8g2 graphics

### Detailed Description

Compiled project with u8g2 SPI to LCD with no optimisation, all data displays correctly.
Change optimisation to Og or above and artifacts appear on the LCD.
Tracked to this file, if all other code is optimised and this file Optimisation set to none, the SPI transfers work correctly and data displays correctly, optimise this file and artifacts appear on the display.


### Expected Behavior

Should behave the same with and without optimisation.

### Actual Behavior

SPI data transfers are corrupted when file is optimised

### Environment

STM32CUBEIDE 2.1.1, gnu-tools-for-stm32.14.3.rel1.win32_1.0.100.202602081740, CUstom PCB with STM32H562 processor

### Severity

Major

Comments:
[BarryAndrews - 2026-05-29T02:48:23Z]
Sorry, relied on Claude too much.  Its possible this is an LCD clock issue when optimised code pumps data quicker. Dropped clock from 15M to 10M and artifacts disappeared.  LCD is rated to 20M but maybe is marginal when SPI pumps data rapidly.

issue_title: [Bug]: NetX Ethernet PTP Transmit Timestamps not Captured
clean_text:
Title: [Bug]: NetX Ethernet PTP Transmit Timestamps not Captured

Body:
### Bug Summary

When _nx_driver_hardware_packet_send() is called with a packet setting NX_INTERFACE_CAPABILITY_PTP_TIMESTAMP, a transmit timestamp isn't captured.

### Detailed Description

Packets setting NX_INTERFACE_CAPABILITY_PTP_TIMESTAMP should capture a timestamp on transmit. For STM32H5 variants with MULTI_QUEUE_FEATURE there is the following code:

C
if (packet_ptr -> nx_packet_interface_capability_flag & NX_INTERFACE_CAPABILITY_PTP_TIMESTAMP)
  {
    HAL_ETH_PTP_InsertTxTimestamp(&eth_handle);
  }


However, no such code exists for variants without MULTI_QUEUE_FEATURE. This means that transmit timestamps aren't captured and HAL_ETH_TxPtpCallback and nx_ptp_client_packet_timestamp_notify are never called, breaking PTP.

To fix this the above code snippet needs to be added [here](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32-mw-netxduo/blob/79232767cef83e20573f2fbc173810f9d29c8fdb/common/drivers/ethernet/nx_stm32_eth_driver.c#L2065).

### Expected Behavior

A timestamp is captured on a packet setting NX_INTERFACE_CAPABILITY_PTP_TIMESTAMP

### Actual Behavior

No timestamp is captured

### Environment

NetXduo

### Severity

Normal

issue_title: [Bug]: HAL RCC VCO computation are incorrect for fractional multiplier
clean_text:
Title: [Bug]: HAL RCC VCO computation are incorrect for fractional multiplier

Body:
### Bug Summary

HAL and LL functions dealing with VCO use floating point numbers that don't have enough precision

### Detailed Description

VCO value maximum value is 560 MHZ (560000000).
This number has 9 decimal digits value in this range requires 32 bits to represent
float variables have on 6-9 decimal digits (fraction part has 23 bits) so it's clear that not all values can be represented.

Lets consider function for calculation of PLL clock for P Q or R
c
uint32_t LL_RCC_CalcPLLClockFreq(uint32_t PLLInputFreq, uint32_t M, uint32_t N, uint32_t FRACN, uint32_t PQR)
{
    float_t freq;

    freq = ((float_t)PLLInputFreq / (float_t)M) * ((float_t)N + ((float_t)FRACN / (float_t)0x2000));

    freq = freq / (float_t)PQR;

    return (uint32_t)freq;
}


While formula is consistent with Datasheet calculated values may be incorrect depending on input values due to float_t being used.

If for example values are as follow

PLLInputFreq = 4000000
M = 1
N = 134
FRACN = 1855
PQR = 2

Returned value is 268437760 Hz
When same function works on double precision numbers result is 268437744 Hz
This gives 16 Hz difference.

I guess double precision computation yields more accurate result.

Here is version that gives same result as double precision computation using 64 bit integers
c
uint32_t LL_RCC_CalcPLLClockFreq(uint32_t PLLInputFreq, uint32_t M, uint32_t N, uint32_t FRACN, uint32_t PQR)
{
    uint64_t freq = (((uint64_t)PLLInputFreq * (N * 0x2000 + FRACN)) / (M * 0x2000)) / PQR;

    return (uint32_t)freq;
}


Other places in **stm32h5xx_hal_rcc.c** also use float numbers for computation and probably also are not accurate.

Same problem applies to stm32h7 devices but those do have double precision floats that could be used instead of integer computation.

Computed frequency difference between current function and double precision/integer computation goes up to 30Hz

### Expected Behavior

_No response_

### Actual Behavior

_No response_

### Environment

_No response_

### Severity

Minor

This issue has been tracked internally.

issue_title: [Bug]: SPI is disabled too early
clean_text:
Title: [Bug]: SPI is disabled too early

Body:
### Bug Summary

When the last (or single) byte of a data transfer has been sent, the SPI is disable too early

### Detailed Description

**SPI disabled to early**

When sending data via SPI, the peripheral is disabled afterwards. some investigation showed that it seems to be disabled to early, while the last clock cycle is still ongoing.

[IMAGE ATTACHED]

Screenshot from oscilloscope shows CH1: SPI1_SCK, CH2: SPI1_MOSI.


Both SPI1_SCK and SPI1_MOSI will fade their signal, instead of perfectly finishing the last bit until the clock will do its falling edge. 

Better to wait for a short time, e.g wait for the TXC complete flag in the SR, and then disable the SPI.

The original code in **stm32h5xx_spi.c** looks like this:
~~~C
static void SPI_CloseTransfer(SPI_HandleTypeDef *hspi)
{
  uint32_t itflag = hspi->Instance->SR;

  __HAL_SPI_CLEAR_EOTFLAG(hspi);
  __HAL_SPI_CLEAR_TXTFFLAG(hspi);

  /* Disable SPI peripheral */
  __HAL_SPI_DISABLE(hspi);
...
~~~

I suggest something similar like the following, to add a check on the TXC flag and a timeout. The code is **not**  yet thoroughly tested and needs to be revised. (Of course we don't like magic numbers, and no blocking loops.)
~~~C
static void SPI_CloseTransfer(SPI_HandleTypeDef *hspi)
{
  uint32_t itflag = hspi->Instance->SR;

  __HAL_SPI_CLEAR_EOTFLAG(hspi);
  __HAL_SPI_CLEAR_TXTFFLAG(hspi);

  /* Disable SPI peripheral */
  int32_t timeout = 1000;
  while ((hspi->Instance->SR & SPI_SR_TXC) == 0) if (--timeout<0) break;
  __HAL_SPI_DISABLE(hspi);
...
~~~

### Expected Behavior

SPI1_SCK to do all 8 cycles of the clock including the last falling edge before it is disable after a complete transfer.

### Actual Behavior

SPI1_SCK does only 7 clock cycles plus an 8th rising edge.

### Environment

NUCLEO-H563ZI, X-NUCLEO-PLC01A1, STM32CubeIDE V2.1.1, STM32CubeMX V6.17, STM32Cube FW_H5 V1.6.0; SPI1: 8bit, 31.25kHz, Clock to SPI 4MHz; HCLK: 250MHz 

### Severity

Normal

clean_text:
Title: [Bug]:  HAL_ETH_PTP_SetTime() adds to the time instead of overwriting it

Body:
### Bug Summary

TSUPDT is used instead of TSINIT to set the timestamp counter value leading to wildly fluctuating timestamps.

### Detailed Description

On [line 1695 of stm32h5xx_hal_eth.c](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h5xx-hal-driver/blob/38ca4af5b1004d3f9e02003ca489df7d065b75ba/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_eth.c#L1695) ETH_MACTSCR_TSUPDT is used to set the timestamp counter, however page 2934 of RM0481 says this bit is used to add or subtract from the timestamp counter instead.

Based on the description of this function, and its use [elsewhere](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32-mw-netxduo/blob/79232767cef83e20573f2fbc173810f9d29c8fdb/common/drivers/ethernet/nx_stm32_eth_driver.c#L2572), this function should instead use ETH_MACTSCR_TSINIT to overwrite the timestamp counter. As it is at the moment, the current time is added to the counter every time there is a PTP sync meaning the time fluctuates wildly over a century and a half span, and the time is never close enough to use fine adjustment methods.

Note: I also put this issue on the [STM Community site](https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-embedded-software/stm32h5-hal-eth-ptp-settime-adds-to-the-time-instead-of/m-p/898661/highlight/true#M75563).

### Expected Behavior

The timestamp counter is set

### Actual Behavior

The timestamp counter is added to

### Environment

_No response_

### Severity

Normal

With Regards,

issue_title: I2C slave sets I2C_CR2_NACK after TX completes, but the peripheral address has already been received for a new transfer
clean_text:
Title: I2C slave sets I2C_CR2_NACK after TX completes, but the peripheral address has already been received for a new transfer

Body:
Hello,

I am experiencing NACKs on the client side when I2C requests (write/read, write/write) are sent repeatedly back to back.

HAL drivers version: v1.5.0-8-g539824f
MCU: STM32H523

The scenario in which the issue can be seen:
The I2C slave has completed transmitting, and the MCU has some work to do and cannot immediately process a new I2C request from a client that is issued immediately after the previous transfer is completed. However, the I2C peripheral has already matched the address of the new request and has set the I2C_FLAG_STOPF flag. When the MCU finally has time to process the I2C interrupt, it calls the function I2C_ITSlaveCplt from the interrupt handler:
c
  /* Check if STOPF is set */
  if ((I2C_CHECK_FLAG(tmpITFlags, I2C_FLAG_STOPF) != RESET) && \
      (I2C_CHECK_IT_SOURCE(ITSources, I2C_IT_STOPI) != RESET))
  {
    /* Call I2C Slave complete process */
    I2C_ITSlaveCplt(hi2c, tmpITFlags);
  }

The function sets the I2C_CR2_NACK flag, which inadvertently stops the active transfer. 

The following workaround does not set the flag if I2C_FLAG_STOPF is set and the logical I2C state is HAL_I2C_STATE_BUSY_TX_LISTEN. The latter condition may not be necessary, though:
diff
diff --git a/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_i2c.c b/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_i2c.c
index 5214c91..8546b1f 100644
--- a/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_i2c.c
+++ b/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_i2c.c
@@ -6582,8 +6582,11 @@ static void I2C_ITSlaveCplt(I2C_HandleTypeDef *hi2c, uint32_t ITFlags)
     /* Do nothing */
   }

-  /* Disable Address Acknowledge */
-  hi2c->Instance->CR2 |= I2C_CR2_NACK;
+  if (I2C_CHECK_FLAG(ITFlags, I2C_FLAG_STOPF) == RESET && tmpstate != HAL_I2C_STATE_BUSY_TX_LISTEN)
+  {
+    /* Disable Address Acknowledge */
+    hi2c->Instance->CR2 |= I2C_CR2_NACK;
+  }

   /* Clear Configuration Register 2 */
   I2C_RESET_CR2(hi2c);

Thank you!

Comments:
[KRASTM - 2025-10-28T11:38:55Z]
Hello @m4083888-blip,

Thank you for bringing this issue to our attention.

I will share it with our team. In the meantime, could you provide us more details, such as:

- Could you please explain more what you mean by I2C requests (write/read, write/write) are sent repeatedly back to back.
- Have you tried using DMA instead of Interrupt, maybe it works fine in your scenario when I2C requests (write/read, write/write) are sent repeatedly back-to-back on the client side.
- Have you tested the workaround long enough? I think it's missing "HAL_I2C_STATE_BUSY_RX_LISTEN" for the receiving case.

With regards,

[m4083888-blip - 2025-10-29T16:47:44Z]
Hello @KRASTM ,

Thank you for looking into it!

By write/read and write/write sequences from a client (master) perspective, I meant the following:
- write address, write register, read register data,
- write address, write register, write register data.

The master sends one of the above requests as soon as the transfer is complete, immediately after it issues the stop bit.

I did consider using DMA; however:
- using DMA might involve some design changes that I wanted to avoid at this point,
- the benefit of using DMA might be negligible in terms of performance since the data part of transfers is usually relatively short.

The workaround was tested by sending over 2 million of the above requests repeatedly.

Checking both HAL_I2C_STATE_BUSY_RX_LISTEN and HAL_I2C_STATE_BUSY_TX_LISTEN makes sense. However, I've never encountered a case where checking these flags had any effect. Just checking the flag I2C_CHECK_FLAG(ITFlags, I2C_FLAG_STOPF) already resolved the issue for me.

[KRASTM - 2025-11-03T13:57:26Z]
ST Internal Reference: 221011

[KRASTM - 2025-11-24T09:46:10Z]

Regarding the issue, our team has decided that there is no plan to implement this change in the near future. However, you can keep the workaround locally since it resolves your problem. I will keep you posted if there are any update.

Thank you in advance for your understanding, please allow me to close the issue.

issue_title: HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA with Linked-List DMA Unintended Behavior
clean_text:
Title: HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA with Linked-List DMA Unintended Behavior

Body:
**Caution**
The Issues are strictly limited for the reporting of problem encountered with the software provided in this project.
For any other problem related to the STM32 product, the performance, the hardware characteristics and boards, the tools the environment in general, please post your report to the ST Community in the STM32 MCUs dedicated [page](https://community.st.com/s/topic/0TO0X000000BSqSWAW/stm32-mcus).

**Describe the set-up**
STM32H573
V1.5.0
Using SPI peripheral with Linked-List DMA

**Describe the bug**
When using SPI with a DMA channel in Linked-List mode, any call to HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA() will set the head node's BNDT register to TxXferCount. This causes unintended behavior where the head node's source/destination addresses is always used for the entirety of the SPI transaction, making it impossible to ever reach any subsequent node in the Linked-List. I believe the user should be the one responsible for configuring their nodes before calling this function.

This also applies to HAL_SPI_TransmiReceive_DMA and HAL_SPI_Receive_DMA.  The line(s) I'm referring to:
[https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h5xx-hal-driver/blob/main/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_spi.c#L2539](url)
[https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h5xx-hal-driver/blob/main/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_spi.c#L2604](url)


Attached is a simple example to describe the issue. Happy to share additional code if it would be helpful. 

To be more clear, the situation is as follows:
1. SPI initialized in slave mode, RX and TX DMA channels linked to SPI, DMA in Linked-List mode
2. Set up nodeA for BNDT=4 bytes and source address=ADDR_A
3. Set up nodeB for BNDT=4 bytes and source address=ADDR_B
4. Call SPI_Transmit_DMA(hspi, ADDR_A, 8) to transmit both buffers
5. I see 8 bytes transferred contiguously starting from ADDR_A, never goes to ADDR_B


[spi_with_linked_list_test.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22179144/spi_with_linked_list_test.txt)

Thank you!

Comments:
[KRASTM - 2025-09-09T08:47:33Z]
Hello @lukewittrup,

Thank you for the report.

Infact, when transfers are done in LinkedList, the transfer size given to HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA() must be the size of the first buffer of the first node. It mustn't be the size of cumulated buffers. HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA() will start the first node and next nodes will be automatically started by DMA at the end of previous node.

The size, source address and destination address of second and third transfer must be defined in configuration of second and third nodes.

With regards,

[KRASTM - 2025-09-17T08:42:52Z]
Hello @lukewittrup,

Please, allow me to close the issue. Thank you in advance for your understanding.

With regards,

    PeriphClkInitStruct.PeriphClockSelection = RCC_PERIPHCLK_RTC;
    PeriphClkInitStruct.RTCClockSelection = RCC_RTCCLKSOURCE_HSE_DIV20;
    if (HAL_RCCEx_PeriphCLKConfig(&PeriphClkInitStruct) != HAL_OK)

* set backup register

Comments:
[ALABSTM - 2024-12-09T16:46:45Z]
Hi @jiri-novotny,

I see you are using a **NUCLEO-H563ZI** board.
* The default configuration for the HSE clock is having it provided the **ST-LINK**. In this case, your application should use RCC_HSE_BYPASS as configuration for clock source instead of RCC_HSE_ON. Pay attention this HSE clock frequency is **8MHz** in this case.
* Otherwise, you have to remove the solder bridge **SB49** to be able to use the **25MHz** external crystal X3 as HSE clock.

Please refer to page **19** or to page **26** of the user manual [UM3115](https://www.st.com/resource/en/user_manual/um3115-stm32h5-nucleo144-board-mb1404-stmicroelectronics.pdf) Rev. 2 for more details.

With regards,

Inc/stm32h5xx_hal_i3c.h:50:3: error: unknown type name 'LL_I3C_CtrlBusConfTypeDef'
   _50 |   LL_I3C_CtrlBusConfTypeDef CtrlBusCharacteristic; /*!< Specifies the I3C controller bus characteristic configuration

Inc/stm32h5xx_hal_i3c.h:1137:62: error: unknown type name 'LL_I3C_CtrlBusConfTypeDef'
 1137 |                                                        const LL_I3C_CtrlBusConfTypeDef *pConfig);
      |                                                              ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Inc/stm32h5xx_hal_i3c.h:1139:61: error: unknown type name 'LL_I3C_TgtBusConfTypeDef'
 1139 |                                                       const LL_I3C_TgtBusConfTypeDef *pConfig);
      |                                                             ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~__

**How to reproduce the bug**

Here's the full compilation command I use for your convenience:
~/arm-gnu-toolchain-13.3.rel1-x86_64-arm-none-eabi/bin/arm-none-eabi-gcc Src/stm32h5xx_ll_i3c.c -o object.o --specs=nosys.specs -std=c17 -mcpu=cortex-m33 -isystem Inc -isystem Inc/Legacy -isystem Include -isystem Device/ST/STM32H5xx/Include -DUSE_FULL_LL_DRIVER -DSTM32H503xx

I implemented stubs for system calls, and added to the include path, in addition to the HAL, the include folders of CMSIS-Core and of the STM32H5xx device.
In addition, I defined USE_HAL_DRIVER in stm32h5xx.h.

**Additional context**

After some investigation, it looks to be a problem with recursive includes.
stm32h5xx_ll_i3c.c ->(includes) **stm32h5xx_ll_i3c.h** -> stm32h5xx.h -> stm32h5xx_hal.h -> stm32h5xx_hal_conf.h -> stm32h5xx_hal_i3c.h -> **stm32h5xx_ll_i3c.h**.

The nested stm32h5xx_ll_i3c.h include is then guarded from being included a second time, while the earlier included stm32h5xx_ll_i3c.h has included stm32h5xx.h before defining the needed  types. Therefore, the including stm32h5xx_hal_i3c.h has unknown type names.

Title: ETH Rx Tailpointer calculation wrong

Body:
**Caution**
The Issues are strictly limited for the reporting of problem encountered with the software provided in this project.
For any other problem related to the STM32 product, the performance, the hardware characteristics and boards, the tools the environment in general, please post your report to the **ST Community** in the STM32 MCUs dedicated [page](https://community.st.com/s/topic/0TO0X000000BSqSWAW/stm32-mcus).

**Describe the set-up**
[NUCLEO-H563ZI](https://www.st.com/en/evaluation-tools/nucleo-h563zi.html) with STM32H563ZIT6

**Describe the bug**
In the function ETH_UpdateDescriptor the calculation of the tailidx/DMACRDTPR is wrong.
Because of this the HAL_ETH_ErrorCallback is reached in my application.
The tail pointer should point to the last built/updated descriptor.

Current (v1.3.0) implementation:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h5xx_hal_driver/blob/0de1dbf8ad03e6e466ed55d1c174656561e3240d/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_eth.c#L1212

Solution to fix the tail pointer:
c
tailidx = (ETH_RX_DESC_CNT + descidx - 1U) % ETH_RX_DESC_CNT;


The related issue in the stm32h7xx_hal_driver reported by Florian-Fischer-InMach:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7xx_hal_driver/issues/61

Body:
File: **Inc/stm32h5xx_ll_rcc.h** (sorry, I'm new to the "issue" section of github and not sure how to find or embed the commit number.)

Lines starting at: 918

The constant: **LL_RCC_USB_CLKSOURCE_PLL2Q** is missing from the file.

When compiling for the NUCLEO-H503RB board, and using the IDE to set the USB clock source to PLL2Q, you will get an undeclared error. The work around is to add:

> #ifndef LL_RCC_USB_CLKSOURCE_PLL2Q
> #define LL_RCC_USB_CLKSOURCE_PLL2Q   RCC_CCIPR4_USBSEL_1       /\*!< PLL2 Q clock used as USB clock source \*/
> #endif

to the "main.h" file.

My best guess as to what is needed to fix the issue, is the lines:

> 918 #define LL_RCC_USB_CLKSOURCE_NONE        0x00000000U               /\*!< No clock used as USB clock source \*/
> 919 #define LL_RCC_USB_CLKSOURCE_PLL1Q       RCC_CCIPR4_USBSEL_0       /\*!< PLL1 Q clock used as USB clock source \*/
> 920 #if defined(RCC_CR_PLL3ON)
> 921 #define LL_RCC_USB_CLKSOURCE_PLL3Q       RCC_CCIPR4_USBSEL_1       /\*!< PLL3 Q clock used as USB clock source \*/
> 922 #endif /\* PLL3 \*/
> 923 #define LL_RCC_USB_CLKSOURCE_HSI48       RCC_CCIPR4_USBSEL         /\*!< HSI48 clock used as USB clock source \*/

should be something like:

> 918 #define LL_RCC_USB_CLKSOURCE_NONE        0x00000000U               /\*!< No clock used as USB clock source \*/
> 919 #define LL_RCC_USB_CLKSOURCE_PLL1Q       RCC_CCIPR4_USBSEL_0       /\*!< PLL1 Q clock used as USB clock source \*/
> 920 #if defined(RCC_CR_PLL3ON)
> 921 #define LL_RCC_USB_CLKSOURCE_PLL3Q       RCC_CCIPR4_USBSEL_1       /\*!< PLL3 Q clock used as USB clock source \*/
> 922 #else
> 923 #define LL_RCC_USB_CLKSOURCE_PLL2Q       RCC_CCIPR4_USBSEL_1       /\*!< PLL2 Q clock used as USB clock source \*/

issue_title: HAL_ADC_Start_DMA gets too slow if temp. channel is used
clean_text:
Title: HAL_ADC_Start_DMA gets too slow if temp. channel is used

Body:
**Describe the set-up**

 * Custom board, using STM32H503CBTx
 * arm-none-eabi-gcc (Arch Repository) 13.2.0

**Describe the bug (skip if none)**

HAL_ADC_Start_DMA get's really slow when internal temp sensor is used on channel that is not strictly related to temperature.


**How to reproduce the bug (skip if none)**

Setup round-robin setup for ADC channels, which at 10kHz does one of the following:
 1) Chann0 is read by DMA for multiple values
 2) Internal temp. is read once

In step 1), usage of HAL_ADC_Start_DMA function is really slow.

The problem disappears if internal temp. channel is not used at all.

**Additional context**

Based on reading of the source code, the problematic place is this:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h5xx_hal_driver/blob/main/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_adc.c#L3519

ADC_Enable will execute the "sensor stabilization delay", which takes a considerable amount of time. (Relative to it being run in 10kHz loop) This seems as waste of time given that the channel being started is NOT the internal temperature channel

Comments:
[RJMSTM - 2024-03-14T07:43:33Z]
Hello @koniarik,

The ADC has been configured to perform two tasks in a 10KHz loop. Firstly, it reads channel 0 using DMA for multiple reads, and secondly, it reads the temperature sensor. This means that the same ADC is being utilized for multiple tasks and is reconfigured each time.
An issue arises when the temperature sensor channel remains active, causing a delay in the stabilization process of the temperature sensor. This delay further causes the ADC to wait when it needs to read channel 0.

To optimize the process, my recommendation would be to disable the temperature sensor when it is not in use. This will prevent any unnecessary delays and ensure that time is not wasted.

Thank you again for your contribution.
With regards,

[koniarik - 2024-03-14T20:52:30Z]
How? And frankly, is it trully the best idea?

My thouhts:
 - The thing is that the this behavior is not exactly clear from the API nor the documentation in adc.c file  (and something I would prefer to be warned about)
 - Suddenly it's not clear to me what is the intended usage of the peripheral... what is the proper way to use it? or what is the proper way to disable just the temperature sensor?
 - Can I do the disable any other way than disabling entire peripheral and enabling again? 
 
 To put it simply: how to disable just the temperature sensor in a way that I can enable it again?

[ARIOSTM - 2024-03-15T14:33:55Z]
Hello @koniarik,

The HAL_ADC_ConfigChannel function automatically enable the temperature sensor when the temperature sensor channel is selected. If you change the configuration the temperature sensor stays enable. You have to manually disable it, if you want to avoid the stabilization time delay.

To disable the temperature sensor when you're not using it you can call  
LL_ADC_SetCommonPathInternalChRem(__LL_ADC_COMMON_INSTANCE(ADC1), LL_ADC_PATH_INTERNAL_TEMPSENSOR);
and enable it again using (it is already automatically done in HAL_ADC_ConfigChannel when temp sensor is selected).
LL_ADC_SetCommonPathInternalChAdd(__LL_ADC_COMMON_INSTANCE(ADC1), LL_ADC_PATH_INTERNAL_TEMPSENSOR);
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h5xx_hal_driver/blob/b21b55fe8b05245d06c559a09a77edf5a0679a74/Inc/stm32h5xx_ll_adc.h#L3199

Best regards

[koniarik - 2024-03-15T15:28:27Z]
I tried to apply the fix but it does not work

I don't have time to investigate this now, as based on my reading of the code it should've worked, I will answer here once I have time for deeper investigation :)

[RJMSTM - 2024-03-21T12:27:48Z]
Hello,
Can you please find the time to test the proposed solution?

I appreciate your honesty and look forward to hearing back from you once you have had the time to conduct a more thorough investigation. In the meantime, please let me know if there is anything I can do to assist you.

Regards, 
Rania

[koniarik - 2024-03-21T17:51:36Z]
Sorry for the way!

Turns out that fix suggested by @ARIOSTM works, there was failure on my side in evaluation.

The proposed fix indeed gets rid of the waiting when different channel is used. It's just that even the wait for temperature channel only switch only, the system is too unresponsive and triggers our internal warnings. But I don't blame that on the HAL, as that is just a property of the temp. sensor.

Thanks!

[RJMSTM - 2024-03-29T10:13:17Z]

Thank you for your feedback, If the solution has resolved your problem, so allow me to close the issue.
We're delighted to hear from you once more.

issue_title: Uninitialised variable: HAL_SD_ConfigWideBusOperation
clean_text:
Title: Uninitialised variable: HAL_SD_ConfigWideBusOperation

Body:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h5xx_hal_driver/blob/b21b55fe8b05245d06c559a09a77edf5a0679a74/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_sd.c#L2373

sdmmc_clk should be initialised to 0U

Comments:
[KRASTM - 2024-01-31T16:26:56Z]
Hello @thyrrestrup,

Thank you for your report.

In fact, the variable "sdmmc_clk" shouldn't be initialized to 0U in the function HAL_SD_ConfigWideBusOperation() To comply to Rule 2.2_c of MISRA C:2012.
Otherwise, the value 0 assigned to "sdmmc_clk" will never be used, as it will be overwritten in one of the Lines below:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h5xx_hal_driver/blob/b21b55fe8b05245d06c559a09a77edf5a0679a74/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_sd.c#L2420-L2429

I Hope this clarified your point and allow me to close the issue.

With Regards

[thyrrestrup - 2024-01-31T18:18:03Z]
arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.2 complain that sdmmc_clk could be used uninitialized. So maybe this should be handled in a different manner then?

If SDMMC2 is not defined then there is no else statement and therefore sdmmc_clk ends up being uninitialized.

[KRASTM - 2024-02-01T16:48:46Z]
Hello @thyrrestrup,

After a double-check we confirm the issue.
Our Dev team has already spotted & fixed it, the fix will be available in the frame of the next release.
Below the details:

* The Local variable "sdmmc_clk" is kept **uninitialized**
* [These](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h5xx_hal_driver/blob/b21b55fe8b05245d06c559a09a77edf5a0679a74/Src/stm32h5xx_hal_sd.c#L2420-L2429) lines of Code have been updated as follow 

diff
    if (hsd->Instance == SDMMC1)
    {
      sdmmc_clk = HAL_RCCEx_GetPeriphCLKFreq(RCC_PERIPHCLK_SDMMC1);
    }
#if defined(SDMMC2)
-    else
+    else if (hsd->Instance == SDMMC2)
    {
      sdmmc_clk = HAL_RCCEx_GetPeriphCLKFreq(RCC_PERIPHCLK_SDMMC2);
    }
#endif /* SDMMC2 */
+    else
+    {
+      sdmmc_clk = 0U;
+    }


Thank you for your feedback, the issue will be kept open until the fix is published on GitHub.
Regards

[thyrrestrup - 2024-02-16T09:44:46Z]
Should this approach also be used in HAL_SD_InitCard?

[KRASTM - 2024-02-19T09:37:39Z]
Hello @Thyrrestrup,

It's not necessary to use the same approach, it's a choice. 

With regards.

[KRASTM - 2024-03-21T11:02:28Z]
Fixed in afcafe6d4f21a18d898400705addd9c94fba8660
